Max Fried and Yankees Blanked Giants in Opener LOWBALL: Athletics Offer Nick Kurtz a Shocking 7-Year, $130M Extension — Fans REACT and Debate Contract Author: WTHR.com staff, CNN Newsource Published: 8:34 PM EDT March 24, 2026 Updated: 8:34 PM EDT March 24, 2026 WASHINGTON — It's called "The Dirty Dozen." It's a list from Environmental Working Group of produce they say contains the most pesticide residue in 2026. Spinach took the top spot, the health advocacy organization said, claiming spinach holds more pesticide residue by weight than any other type of produce. The rest of the list includes kale, collard and mustard greens, strawberries, grapes, nectarines, peaches, cherries, apples, blackberries, pears and blueberries. EWG has issued the report each year since 2004. For the first time, the report found more than 60% of the Dirty Dozen samples contained pesticides known as "forever chemicals" called PFAs. The name comes from research that says the chemicals can take decades, even centuries, to fully break down in the environment.
